description: The conformance corpus for standards/027-json-document-storage.md. Four parts. 'admissions' is judged by admission.schema.json, plus four checks the schema cannot express and the runner makes, each case saying which judged it in 'judgedBy': the engine's admitted roles against storage-profiles.json, that current_schema_version has a schema, that the runtime and declaration credentials differ, and that every index on a scoped collection leads with the outermost isolation field. 'envelopes' is judged by document-envelope.schema.json, plus two checks made against the collection each case names: a scoped collection's document must carry tenant_id, and a document must be within its collection's max_document_bytes ('bytes' gives the serialised size where it matters). 'evolution' is judged by running a reader (DS6): given a fixture naming each version's required and optional fields and a reader whose window is the current version and the one before it, each document is accepted, upgraded to the current version with defaults applied, or refused with a named reason; unknown fields are ignored and listed. One case is a detector: a current-version document carrying a field the schema does not list, which a reader that closes its schema refuses while passing every other case. 'rollouts' is judged by simulating deployments (DS6's three-release rule): each step deploys a release that writes one version and accepts a set, or backfills the store to a version; a deploy is a rolling one, so the previous release's reader is live while the new release writes; the sequence is unsafe at the first step where a live reader would meet a version it refuses, either from the other live release's writer or from the store after rollout.

envelopes.why: DS5 in full: the five fields, a UUIDv7 id, canonical instants, a body beyond the envelope.
DS5: tenant_id is absent only where the admission marks the collection unscoped, and this one is.

DS4: a scoped collection's document carries tenant_id or it is invisible to every isolation predicate and visible to a missed one. The envelope schema cannot know the collection is scoped; the runner reads the collection and refuses.
IP1 through DS4: an integer is an internal key, or an engine's counter, and neither is a public id.

envelopes.schemaCannotCatch: DS4's rule against the engine's generated identifier. A 24-character hex ObjectId is a well-formed nanoid to the IP2 pattern, and no schema can tell them apart. Recorded as passing so the file does not imply coverage it lacks; the admission's id_source and the review question are the gate.

envelopes.why: IP4 through DS5: stored instants are UTC with a Z suffix at the pinned precision. An offset form makes equal instants unequal strings.
DS6: a document that does not say which schema it was written under cannot be read except on a guess, and a guess is a corruption on the next write.
DS6: versions start at 1. Zero is the value a serialiser writes for an unset integer, which is a missing version wearing a number.
DS5: the envelope is open. The body is the collection's own schema's business, and an envelope that closed itself would forbid every document from having content.

DS10: the collection's ceiling is 64 KiB and this document serialises to 3 MiB. It is a blob that escaped its standard, and the writer refuses it rather than truncating it. The schema cannot weigh a document; the runner compares bytes to the collection's ceiling.

evolution.why: DS6: the version the writer writes, every required field present and typed.
DS6: the reader accepts N-1 and supplies N's defaults on read. It does not rewrite the document; the backfill (DS7) does.

DS6 and PC6, and a VERIFIED DETECTOR. Within a version, change is additive: a newer writer of the same version added an optional field this reader has not been taught. A reader that closes its schema - additionalProperties false against the version's field list - refuses this document and passes every other case in this part. That reader has made every additive change a breaking one, and this case fails it by name.
DS6: a version above the window may carry a required field whose meaning the reader cannot know. It is refused with the version named, never read on a guess.
DS6 / DS7: a reader at 3 accepts 3 and 2. A version-1 document is one the backfill should have rewritten before acceptance of 1 was dropped, and refusing it is what makes that omission visible.
DS6: the document claims version 2 and lacks a field version 2 requires. It is not a version-1 document mislabelled; it is a document that fails its own schema, and the reader says which field.
DS5 / DS6: the envelope is checked before the body. A document with no version is not assumed to be the current one.
DS6: the reader validates against the version's schema before the body of any handler runs (057 JB1's rule applied to a document). A retyped field is a new version, not a tolerated variant.

rollouts.why: DS6's three releases, in order: accept the new version, then write it and backfill, then drop the old one. At no step does a live reader meet a version it refuses.

DS6 / SD4's reason: during r2's rolling deployment r1's replicas are still reading, and r2 is writing a version r1 refuses. The release fails during its own rollout, and the rollback to r1 fails the same way against what r2 wrote.
DS6 / DS7: the store still holds version-1 documents because the backfill never ran to nothing-left, and r4 refuses them. The third release waits for the backfill's report, not for the calendar.
DS6 / PC6: an optional field is added within the version. r1's readers ignore it (the evolution detector), r2's readers know it, and nothing changes hands.
